summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic lymphedema, morbid obesity, and a history of recurrent cellulitis was admitted with altered mental status and worsening bilateral lower extremity pain and redness. She was found to be confused and cold to the touch at her nursing home. Though blood cultures remained negative, she met clinical criteria for sepsis, likely due to Pseudomonas from cellulitis, and was treated with intravenous antibiotics including vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam, later transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin. Her mental status improved, consistent with resolution of metabolic encephalopathy. A CT scan showed no abscess but worsening skin thickening and edema. She responded well to treatment, with stabilization of vital signs and labs. She was discharged on oral antibiotics with plans for ongoing lymphedema management and close outpatient follow-up.
problems: Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of other female genital organs
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
